thread:
Sophie (FinOps): FYI noticed ~42 invoices marked 'webhook failed' in our daily reconcile. All from last night window (00:00-01:30 UTC). server says NetSuite consumer DLQ.

Raj (Backend): Hmm — do we have a sample webhook id?

Sophie (FinOps): One example: wh_1Jk8cXabc123. NetSuite-Worker logs: \"Malformed header: Unknown charset 'usascii'\", followed by json parse error.

stripe-bot: Delivered webhook wh_1Jk8cXabc123 to /integrations/stripe/webhook-proxy at 2026-03-18T00:12:43Z (200 OK)

Lena (Billing-Eng): Can you paste the raw headers/body from the DLQ for that event?

Sophie (FinOps): Copied snippet from DLQ: 
```
POST /integrations/stripe/webhook-proxy
Content-Type: application/json; charset=US-ASCII
Stripe-Signature: t=1700000000,v1=abc123
{\n  \"id\": \"evt_1Jk8b...\",\n  \"data\": { ... },\n  \"lines\": [{\"sku\": \"AC-XL\", \"qty\": 1}]\n}
```

Raj (Backend): That nonprintable (\u001F) in SKU looks like binary/encoding munging. Our stripe-proxy assumes utf-8 and passthroughs Content-Type. NetSuite consumer uses strict UTF-8 validation — will DLQ on unknown charset or control chars.

Marta (Finance Ops): Does Stripe ever send US-ASCII? We haven't changed anything upstream.

Lena (Billing-Eng): Stripe always sends UTF-8 by default; but some older integrations or SDKs may set charset=US-ASCII. More likely a legacy client or middleware re-encoding. We should normalize before handing to netsuite worker.

Raj (Backend): Agreed. Quick mitigation: 1) webhook-proxy should coerce body -> UTF-8 and strip control chars from SKU fields; 2) for charset header, override to \"application/json; charset=utf-8\"; 3) push to staging then prod. I'll open a small patch.

Raj (Backend): Patch sketch: 
```python
# in stripe_proxy/handlers.py
raw = request.get_data()
try:
  body = raw.decode('utf-8')
except UnicodeDecodeError:
  body = raw.decode('latin-1').encode('utf-8').decode('utf-8', 'replace')
# sanitize SKU field
body = re.sub(r"[\\x00-\\x1F&&[^\\n\\r\\t]]+", "", body)
request.headers['Content-Type'] = 'application/json; charset=utf-8'
```

Lena (Billing-Eng): Also we need to ensure idempotency keys are preserved so replays/backfills don't create duplicate invoices. The NetSuite worker uses event.id as idempotency token — confirm the proxy isn't dropping it.

Raj (Backend): Good call. Proxy currently forwards all headers except a few. I'll add a test to assert Stripe-Signature and X-Event-ID (we rely on event.id).

NetSuite-Worker: DLQ consumer log for wh_1Jk8cXabc123: \"Rejecting event evt_1Jk8b...: charset 'US-ASCII' not supported; control char in sku 'AC\\u001F-XL'\"

Marta (Finance Ops): Operational ask — can we backfill the failed window? We need those invoices in NetSuite before month close.

Lena (Billing-Eng): Yes. Two-step plan: 1) deploy quick normalization fix to stripe-proxy (hotfix, low-risk) 2) run backfill script to reprocess DLQ + re-ingest webhooks from the failed window with dedupe checks.

Raj (Backend): I'll draft the PR and include tests + metric (dlq.count per hour). Can we schedule a short deploy at 09:30 PST?

Sophie (FinOps): 09:30 PST works. Please add a rollback plan. Also notify accounting to expect ~42 invoices to appear again.

Lena (Billing-Eng): Backfill command (internal): 
```
./scripts/replay_webhooks.py --source dlq --since 2026-03-18T00:00:00Z --until 2026-03-18T02:00:00Z --dry-run
./scripts/replay_webhooks.py --source dlq --dedupe --commit
```

Raj (Backend): I'll attach a unit test, the PR link, and the deploy runbook here when ready.

Sophie (FinOps): Thanks. One more thing — can we add a quick monitoring alert: DLQ spike > 5 in 1h for stripe events? We missed this earlier.

Lena (Billing-Eng): Will add alert to rb_alerts: stripe_dlq_count > 5 in 1h -> paging to oncall and post to #finance-incidents.

Marta (Finance Ops): TY both. Will hold off on manual adjustments until deploy + backfill completes.

Raj (Backend): PR: https://internal.redwood/dev/stripe-proxy/pulls/412 (WIP). Leaving deploy notes in the runbook.

Sophie (FinOps): Great. Keep this thread updated after the deploy + backfill. :thumbsup:
